The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that lets large
language models (LLMs) securely interact with external data and applications.
The Google Ads MCP server provides a standardized bridge to the Google Ads API. It lets
AI agents retrieve and analyze account data, create assets, upload videos, and
manage labels by using natural language. Community resources and support GitHub repository: Find demos and examples, report bugs, or suggest
features in the google-ads-mcp repository . Use the Issues tab for bug reports and feature requests. Community: Join the #ads-api-ai-tools channel on the Google
Advertising Community Discord . Technical overview Integrating the Google Ads MCP server removes the need to write custom code for
Google Ads API authentication, resource fetching, data parsing, and supported asset or
label mutations. The server exposes callable tools and reference resources (see Core capabilities ) that an LLM
can inspect and invoke. Key specifications Protocol: MCP (Model Context Protocol) Mode: Read and partial mutate (asset creation, video uploads, and label
management with propose-and-confirm validation , or configurable read-only mode ) Language: Python 3.10 or later Transport: Standard input/output ( stdio ) or Streamable HTTP
( streamable-http on Cloud Run) Authentication: Application Default Credentials (OAuth 2.0 user
credentials or service account) for local stdio , or OAuth 2.0 Web
application credentials for remote HTTP Telemetry: Appends google-ads-mcp/VERSION to the x-goog-api-client gRPC request header for usage statistics How the interaction loop works Request: You submit a prompt such as "How is my campaign performance
this week?" or "Create a callout asset for our summer sale" . Discovery: The LLM inspects its available tools and resources and
selects a matching google-ads-mcp tool. Execution or dry-run validation: Read tools query the Google Ads API directly.
Mutate tools first run in propose mode ( validate_only=True ) to validate
inputs without committing changes (see Propose-and-confirm safety
workflow ). Context injection: The MCP server returns structured query results, or
proposed change_items entries and a verification checksum digest, to the
LLM's context window. Response and confirmation: The LLM presents an answer or asks you to
confirm the proposed changes. After you approve, the LLM calls the mutate
tool again with validate_only=False and the matching checksum value to
commit the change. Get started Follow these steps to configure and run the Google Ads MCP server locally. To deploy
a shared remote service instead, see Deployment on Google
Cloud . Prerequisites Before you configure the server, complete the following prerequisites in your
local environment and the Google Cloud console : Google Cloud project: Create or select a Google Cloud project with the
Google Ads API enabled. Enabling the API grants Test access for testing read
and mutate workflows against test accounts . To access
production accounts, check the Google Ads API overview page for
Explorer, Basic, or Standard access, or apply for one of these access
levels . Otherwise, production calls fail with an AuthorizationError.CLOUD_PROJECT_NOT_APPROVED_FOR_PRODUCTION error. Google
sunset developer tokens ( GOOGLE_ADS_DEVELOPER_TOKEN ) on
September 9, 2026. The Google Cloud project that owns your OAuth client or
service account determines your API access level. Credentials: Local stdio mode authenticates with Application Default
Credentials (ADC) from an OAuth 2.0 client secret JSON file or a
service account in your Cloud project. Set the GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT environment variable when needed to specify your default quota or ADC
project. Remote streamable-http deployments instead require an OAuth 2.0
Web application Client ID and Client secret (see Deploy to Google Cloud
Run ). Local software (for stdio mode): Install Python 3.10 or
later , pipx , and the gcloud command-line
tool (used to generate user ADC files). Configuration Generate Application Default Credentials (ADC) using an OAuth
client from your API-enabled Google Cloud project and include the Google Ads API
scope: gcloud auth application-default login \ --scopes = https://www.googleapis.com/auth/adwords,https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \ --client-id-file = PATH_TO_CLIENT_SECRET_JSON Replace the following: PATH_TO_CLIENT_SECRET_JSON : the path to your OAuth 2.0 client secret
JSON file. This command prints Credentials saved to file: [PATH_TO_CREDENTIALS_JSON] (such as ~/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json on Linux
and macOS). To authenticate with a service account instead, skip this step
and point GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS to your service account key JSON
file, or pass --impersonate-service-account to gcloud auth
application-default login . Add the server to your host's MCP configuration file (such as ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json , ~/.gemini/settings.json , or ~/.claude/settings.json ): { "mcpServers" : { "google-ads-mcp" : { "command" : "pipx" , "args" : [ "run" , "--spec" , "google-ads-mcp==0.0.6" , "google-ads-mcp" ], "env" : { "GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT" : "PROJECT_ID" , "GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS" : "PATH_TO_CREDENTIALS_JSON" } } } } Replace the following: PROJECT_ID : your Google Cloud project ID. PATH_TO_CREDENTIALS_JSON : the path to the ADC JSON file printed in
step 1, or to your service account key JSON file. You can omit GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS when using the default gcloud ADC
file location. To access client accounts through a manager account, set GOOGLE_ADS_LOGIN_CUSTOMER_ID (10 digits, without hyphens) in env , or
pass the login_customer_id parameter on individual tool calls. Tip: For faster startup, install the package once with pipx install
google-ads-mcp and set "command": "google-ads-mcp" (with "args": [] ). When
a new Google Ads API version such as v26.2 is released, run pipx upgrade
google-ads-mcp (or pipx run --no-cache ) to update the bundled google-ads Python client library to 35.x+ . Optional: Equip your agent with skills and the Developer Assistant The Google Ads MCP server gives your AI client live access to account reporting
data along with asset creation, video upload, and label management tools. Pair
the MCP server with the following companion tools to help your agent construct
valid Google Ads Query Language (GAQL) queries and diagnose account
performance shifts. These tools also generate client library code, such as
scripts to link created assets to campaigns or perform other unsupported
mutations: Google Ads API AI agent skills: Portable workflow modules (including google-ads-api-mcp-setup , google-ads-api-account-diagnostics , and google-ads-api-quickstart ) that help your agent use the Google Ads MCP server
with lower token overhead. Run the following command to install them
(requires Node.js ), or see the Google Ads API AI agent skills
guide for Antigravity, Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor setup: npx skills add google/skills/skills/ads Google Ads API Developer Assistant: An open-source plugin (not an officially
supported Google product) for Google Antigravity and Claude Code that
provides local Protobuf schema inspection, GAQL validation, client library
code generation, and offline conversion troubleshooting. See Choose the right Google Ads AI tool or follow the installation guide . Core capabilities The following sections describe the server's read tools, partial mutate tools,
and reference resources. Starting in v0.0.6 , tools register by default with
their category namespace prefix (such as search_search ). When upgrading
prompts or allowlists from unprefixed releases, update tool names or set an
empty prefix ( "" ) in tools_config.yaml (see Configure tool namespaces and
read-only mode ). Read tools customers_list_accessible_customers (tool list_accessible_customers ): Returns the Google Ads customer IDs directly
accessible to the authenticated user. search_search (tool search ): Builds and runs GAQL SearchStream queries from structured parameters ( customer_id , resource , and fields , plus optional conditions , orderings , limit ,
and login_customer_id ) rather than a raw GAQL string. Every query appends PARAMETERS omit_unselected_resource_names=true to fetch resource
attributes, metrics, segments, budgets, and status cleanly. metadata_get_resource_metadata (tool get_resource_metadata ):
Retrieves selectable, filterable, and sortable attributes, metrics, and
segments for a Google Ads API resource type (for example, "campaign" ). Use this
metadata to discover valid query fields—including metrics and segments added
in minor releases such as v26.2—before calling the search_search tool. Mutate tools (partial support) assets_create_asset (tool create_asset ): Creates standalone Google Ads
assets with dedicated parameters for TEXT , IMAGE , YOUTUBE_VIDEO , SITELINK , CALLOUT , and STRUCTURED_SNIPPET asset
types. Pass the extra_params dictionary for other mutable AssetService types (such as PRICE , PROMOTION , CALL , or BUSINESS_MESSAGE ), and
include root-level final_urls alongside sitelink_link_text for SITELINK assets. Local file paths ( image_asset_path ) work in local stdio mode only. For remote HTTP deployments, pass the base64-encoded image_asset_data parameter with image_asset_mime_type set to IMAGE_PNG , IMAGE_JPEG , or IMAGE_GIF (up to 20 MB). assets_upload_video_asset (tool upload_video_asset ): Uploads a
local video file ( .3gp , .avi , .flv , .mkv , .mov , .mp4 , .mpeg , .mpg , .ogg , .webm , or .wmv ) to YouTube through the
Google Ads API as a FastMCP background task in local stdio mode only. Both video_title and video_description are required parameters. The video_privacy parameter accepts UNLISTED (default) or PUBLIC (allowed
only on advertiser-owned brand channels with user OAuth). This tool returns
a Google Ads video_upload_id value (and resource name), not the 11-character
YouTube video_id . Query you_tube_video_upload with the search_search tool (filtering by you_tube_video_upload.video_upload_id ) until you_tube_video_upload.state = 'PROCESSED' . Then pass you_tube_video_upload.video_id as the youtube_video_id parameter to assets_create_asset ( asset_type="YOUTUBE_VIDEO" ). labels_manage_labels (tool manage_labels ): Creates, updates, and
removes account labels, including name, description, and hex background
color. labels_manage_label_associations (tool manage_label_associations ):
Supports CREATE and REMOVE label association operations ( UPDATE is not
supported) on CAMPAIGN , CUSTOMER , AD_GROUP , and AD_GROUP_CRITERION resources. For CUSTOMER resources, resource_id is optional and defaults
to customer_id . Pass a composite {ad_group_id}~{criterion_id} ID for AD_GROUP_CRITERION resources, and remove associations by passing either resource_id and label_id or association_resource_name . Ad-level AD_GROUP_AD labels are not supported. Note: Mutate support covers standalone asset creation, video uploads, and label
management only. The server cannot link assets to campaigns, ad groups, or asset
groups, or configure ad-level asset automation settings (such as OVERLAY_TEXT_ON_VIDEOS in v26.2). It also cannot create, modify, pause, or
enable campaigns, ad groups, ads, budgets, or bids. For unsupported mutations,
pair the server with companion code-generation tools (see Equip your agent with
skills and the Developer Assistant ). Reference resources The server exposes four read-only MCP resources that remain mounted regardless
of your tools_config.yaml settings: resource://discovery-document : JSON REST discovery overview of Google Ads API
resources, service methods, and schemas. It complements the metadata_get_resource_metadata tool, which returns selectable, filterable,
and sortable GAQL query fields. resource://metrics : HTML reference documentation for Google Ads API metrics. resource://segments : HTML reference documentation for Google Ads API
segments. resource://release-notes : HTML Google Ads API release notes covering version
changes and new features. Propose-and-confirm safety workflow Every mutate tool ( assets_create_asset , assets_upload_video_asset , labels_manage_labels , and labels_manage_label_associations ) enforces a
two-step propose-and-confirm workflow to help prevent unintended account
modifications: Propose ( validate_only=True , default): Validates inputs without
committing changes. The asset and label tools execute a live Google Ads API validate_only dry run. Because YouTubeVideoUploadService has no dry-run
mode, assets_upload_video_asset instead validates the local file and binds
its size and modification timestamp. Each tool returns human-readable change_items entries and a stateless SHA-256 checksum digest bound to
the customer_id parameter and request payload. Confirm ( validate_only=False ): After presenting the change_items list and receiving your approval, the agent calls the tool again with validate_only=False , the identical customer_id parameter and arguments,
and the checksum value from step 1. The server rejects any missing or
mismatched checksum before mutating the account. Note: The checksum value is an unkeyed SHA-256 digest of the request
parameters that works statelessly across Cloud Run instances. It prevents
accidental parameter drift or local file swaps across turns, but does not
replace access control. To hard-block mutations, disable the labels and assets namespaces in tools_config.yaml . Configure tool namespaces and read-only mode The server bundles a default tools_config.yaml file with all five tool
categories ( customers , search , metadata , labels , and assets ) enabled.
Customize tools_config.yaml to selectively enable or disable individual tools
or namespaces, change or remove namespace prefixes, or enforce a strictly
read-only deployment. Important: Whenever namespaces is non-empty, any omitted category is
disabled by default , whereas an empty namespaces: {} mapping enables all
five categories. Include every category that you want to keep enabled—a file
containing only labels: false and assets: false disables the read tools too. At startup, the server resolves tools_config.yaml in the following order: An explicit path in the GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_TOOLS_CONFIG environment variable
(recommended for local stdio hosts, whose working directory can differ
from your project folder). A tools_config.yaml file in the server's current working directory. The default tools_config.yaml file bundled with the package. If GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_TOOLS_CONFIG points to a missing file, or if any resolved
configuration file is invalid, the server raises an error at startup instead of
falling back to defaults. The following minimal tools_config.yaml file enforces a strictly read-only
deployment: namespaces : customers : true search : true metadata : true labels : false assets : false The following tools_config.yaml file customizes prefixes and filters
individual tools (for example, exposing the base64 create_asset tool on Cloud
Run while disabling the local-only upload_video_asset tool): namespaces : # Default prefix ("customers_list_accessible_customers") customers : true # Empty prefix mounts unprefixed tool names ("search") search : "" # Custom prefix ("schema_get_resource_metadata") metadata : "schema" # Enable only specific tools in a multi-tool category assets : enabled_tools : - create_asset Sample prompts to start Try the following prompts in your MCP client after connecting the server. Ask what the server can do What can the google-ads-mcp server do? Ask about customers What customers do I have access to? Ask about campaigns How many active campaigns do I have? How is my campaign performance this week? Give me a report of the top spending campaigns split by device category over the last 7 days for account 1234567890 Create assets, upload videos, and manage labels Create a callout asset with the text "Free Shipping" for account 1234567890 Upload /path/to/promo.mp4 with title "Summer Sale" and description "Summer promo video" for account 1234567890 Create a label named "Q4 Promo" with background color #34A853 and apply it to campaign 9876543210 in account 1234567890 Note: Video uploads require local stdio mode. Creating a new label and
applying it to a campaign runs two sequential propose-and-confirm cycles so the
new label_id value can be validated in the association request. Deployment on Google Cloud To share the MCP server across multiple agents or run it as a web service, host
it on Google Cloud Run or another cloud infrastructure provider instead of
running it locally. Prerequisites A Google Cloud project with the Google Ads API enabled (see Prerequisites for production access requirements). The gcloud command-line tool installed, authenticated, and
configured with an active project: gcloud config set project PROJECT_ID Replace the following: PROJECT_ID : your Google Cloud project ID. Build and push a Docker image Use Cloud Build to build and push the container image to Artifact Registry
without installing Docker locally: Create a repository in Artifact Registry: gcloud artifacts repositories create mcp-servers \ --repository-format = docker --location = us-central1 Build and submit the image from a release tag in the GitHub repository (or
from . in a local checkout if you customized Dockerfile or tools_config.yaml ): gcloud builds submit https://github.com/googleads/google-ads-mcp \ --git-source-revision = v0.0.6 \ --tag = us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT_ID/mcp-servers/google-ads-mcp:v0.0.6 Replace the following: PROJECT_ID : your Google Cloud project ID. Rebuild and redeploy the image whenever you update google-ads-mcp or
upgrade the bundled google-ads Python client library for new Google Ads API
releases (such as v26.2). Deploy to Google Cloud Run Configure the following environment variables and secrets for your Cloud Run
service: GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID : The OAuth 2.0 Web application Client
ID from your API-enabled Google Cloud project for application-level OAuth
authentication. Complete the following OAuth configuration steps: Add the authorized redirect URIs for any AI clients that you plan to
connect (such as https://claude.ai/api/mcp/auth_callback , https://chatgpt.com/connector_platform_oauth_redirect , or https://antigravity.google/oauth-callback ). Add the https://www.googleapis.com/auth/adwords scope to the OAuth
consent screen under APIs & Services > OAuth consent screen > Data
Access ( Add or remove scopes ). If your OAuth consent screen publishing status is set to Testing (the default), add the Google Accounts connecting to the MCP server as Test users under APIs & Services > OAuth consent screen >
Audience ( Test users > + Add users ). GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET : The OAuth Client secret corresponding
to your OAuth Client ID. GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_BASE_URL : The public base URL of your MCP server (for
example, https://google-ads-mcp-xyz-uc.a.run.app ). Cloud Run assigns this
URL during initial deployment, so deploy without this variable first and
update the service afterward. GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_JWT_SIGNING_KEY (recommended for multi-instance Cloud
Run) : A persistent secret that signs FastMCP JWTs across container restarts
and horizontal scaling. GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_STORAGE_TYPE (recommended for multi-instance Cloud Run) :
Backend for OAuth client registrations and tokens. Supported values are redis , firestore , filetree (with GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_STORAGE_PATH for
non-Cloud Run VM or mounted-volume deployments), and memory . Setting a
backend-specific variable selects that backend even if GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_STORAGE_TYPE is unset. When all GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_STORAGE_* backend variables are unset, FastMCP uses its default container-local
storage; for single-instance testing with local or memory storage, pass --max-instances=1 : redis : Set GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_STORAGE_REDIS_URL (defaults to redis://localhost:6379/0 ) and install py-key-value-aio[redis] in a
custom Dockerfile . Redis expires entries automatically. firestore : Optionally set GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_STORAGE_FIRESTORE_PROJECT (defaults to the ADC project)
and GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_STORAGE_FIRESTORE_DATABASE (defaults to (default) ). Install .[firestore] in a custom Dockerfile , provision
a Firestore database, and grant the roles/datastore.user Identity and
Access Management (IAM) role to the Cloud Run service account. The
Firestore store filters expired entries on read without deleting them.
Because it stores expires_at as a string, Firestore time to live (TTL)
policies can't delete expired entries. For long-running deployments,
plan periodic cleanup or use Redis. memory : Ephemeral in-memory storage (useful only with --max-instances=1 ). GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY (optional) : Dedicated Fernet
encryption key (or high-entropy secret) for stored OAuth state. This setting
and GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_STORAGE_DISABLE_ENCRYPTION=true apply only when an
explicit GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_STORAGE_* backend is configured. If omitted, the
server derives an encryption key from GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_JWT_SIGNING_KEY , or
falls back to GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET when no JWT signing key
is set. Setting a dedicated encryption key prevents rotating that fallback
secret from invalidating stored OAuth tokens. PORT (optional) : Listening port in streamable-http mode (defaults to 8080 ; Cloud Run sets this automatically). GOOGLE_ADS_LOGIN_CUSTOMER_ID (optional) : Default 10-digit manager
customer ID (without hyphens) used when tool calls omit the login_customer_id parameter. GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_TOOLS_CONFIG (optional) : Container path to a custom tools_config.yaml file (for example, mounted from Secret Manager at /etc/mcp/tools_config.yaml to enforce read-only mode without rebuilding
the image). See Configure tool namespaces and read-only
mode . Store GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET and GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_JWT_SIGNING_KEY in Secret Manager and deploy the service to Google Cloud Run: gcloud run deploy google-ads-mcp \ --image = us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT_ID/mcp-servers/google-ads-mcp:v0.0.6 \ --platform = managed \ --region = us-central1 \ --allow-unauthenticated \ --set-env-vars = "GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=CLIENT_ID" \ --set-secrets = "GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=MCP_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET:latest,GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_JWT_SIGNING_KEY=MCP_JWT_SIGNING_KEY:latest" After Cloud Run completes the deployment, retrieve the assigned service URL and
update the service with the GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_BASE_URL environment variable: gcloud run services update google-ads-mcp \ --region = us-central1 \ --update-env-vars = "GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_BASE_URL=https://CLOUD_RUN_SERVICE_URL" Replace the following: PROJECT_ID : your Google Cloud project ID. CLIENT_ID : your OAuth 2.0 Web application Client ID. MCP_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET : the Secret Manager secret name storing your
OAuth 2.0 Client secret. MCP_JWT_SIGNING_KEY : the Secret Manager secret name storing your JWT
signing key. CLOUD_RUN_SERVICE_URL : the hostname assigned to your Cloud Run service
(for example, google-ads-mcp-xyz-uc.a.run.app ). Authentication and security model Deploying with --allow-unauthenticated disables Cloud Run's infrastructure IAM
check ( roles/run.invoker ) so external AI clients can connect without Google
Cloud service account tokens. Authentication is delegated to the application
layer instead: When GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET are set, the server enforces Google
OAuth 2.0 on every request and returns a 401 Unauthorized HTTP status code
to unauthenticated callers. Every tool call executes under the authenticated
caller's OAuth identity. Omitting --allow-unauthenticated requires callers to pass Google Cloud
OIDC identity tokens with every request. Standard AI clients (such as Claude
and ChatGPT) use end-user OAuth rather than Google Cloud IAM tokens, so
direct connections require --allow-unauthenticated paired with
application-level OAuth. Caution: Never omit GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_ADS_MCP_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET when deploying with --allow-unauthenticated . Those environment variables switch the server from
local stdio mode to streamable-http transport. Without them, the server
falls back to Application Default Credentials (ADC) and exposes the container's
service account credentials to unauthenticated callers. Configure the MCP client After deployment, configure your MCP client with the Cloud Run service URL.
Because the server enforces OAuth 2.0, your client must support the MCP OAuth
flow or supply an authorized Bearer token: OAuth-enabled clients: In clients that support MCP OAuth discovery (such
as Antigravity), connecting triggers a Google sign-in prompt to grant the https://www.googleapis.com/auth/adwords scope (shown as .../auth/adwords in the Google Cloud console). Third-party AI platforms (Claude, ChatGPT): In your client's connector
settings, add a custom connector pointing to your service URL with the /mcp path (for example, https://google-ads-mcp-xyz-uc.a.run.app/mcp ).
Select OAuth 2.0 authentication with your OAuth Client ID and Client secret,
and confirm that the client's callback URI is in your OAuth client's
authorized redirect URIs. Clients without OAuth support: Clients that don't support HTTP OAuth
flows receive a 401 Unauthorized HTTP status code. For those clients, use
the local stdio configuration instead. The following example configures the gemini command-line tool in ~/.gemini/settings.json (for Google Antigravity in ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json , replace "httpUrl" with "serverUrl" or "url" ): { "mcpServers" : { "google-ads-mcp" : { "httpUrl" : "https://CLOUD_RUN_SERVICE_URL/mcp" } } } Replace the following: CLOUD_RUN_SERVICE_URL : the hostname assigned to your Cloud Run service
(for example, google-ads-mcp-xyz-uc.a.run.app ).
